title: Returning a Wallet Found After the Prayer
script: Imam Khalid: [thoughtful] Imam Khalid, I found this wallet near the mosque entrance after the prayer. It has cash and identification inside.
Faris: Thank you for bringing it here. Let us avoid opening more than is necessary to identify the owner and protect the property.
Imam Khalid: [carefully] Should I announce the name and amount so the owner comes quickly?
Faris: No. A public description can invite a false claim. We can announce that an item was found and ask a claimant to describe distinguishing details privately.
Imam Khalid: [reflective] There is an address on the identification card. Should I go there tonight?

Faris: First consider safety, local procedure, and whether the person may prefer contact through an official channel. The mosque can keep a documented found-property record and contact the owner carefully.
Imam Khalid: [honestly] What if someone says it is theirs but cannot describe the cash amount?
Faris: We should not reveal the amount first. Ask about the wallet, cards, marks, and other details, then compare them with the record. If doubt remains, use appropriate authorities.
Imam Khalid: [seriously] Can I keep it until someone claims it, since I found it?
Faris: No. Found property is an amanah, not a reward. It needs secure custody, a clear record, and reasonable efforts to return it under local law and mosque policy.
Imam Khalid: [gently] What happens if nobody claims it?
Faris: The policy and relevant law guide the next step. We should not invent a rule or use the money personally without authority.
Imam Khalid: [encouraging] I will record the time, location, condition, and identifying features, then give it to the authorized custodian.
Faris: Good. Do not post images of the identification or cash, and do not tell a crowd private details about the owner.
Imam Khalid: [sincere] I was tempted to solve it quickly by posting everything online.
Faris: Quick publicity can create theft, embarrassment, or fraud. A careful process may feel slower, but it protects the owner’s rights.
Imam Khalid: [thoughtful] Thank you. I understand that returning property includes guarding it while it is still missing.
Faris: Exactly. Honesty is not only handing something back; it is protecting it from the moment it reaches your hand.

quiz.question: Why is the owner’s name not announced?
options: It could help a false claimant

quiz.question: What should a claimant provide?
options: Private distinguishing details that can be compared with the record

quiz.question: Why cannot Faris keep the wallet?
options: Found property is a trust requiring secure authorized custody

quiz.question: What if nobody claims it?
options: Follow mosque policy and applicable law

quiz.question: What does honesty include here?
options: Protecting the wallet from loss or fraud before return

quiz.question: What record should Faris make?
options: Time, location, condition, and identifying features

quiz.question: Why avoid wallet photographs online?
options: They may expose identity and invite theft or fraud

quiz.question: Who receives the wallet for safekeeping?
options: The authorized custodian under mosque policy

quiz.question: What does the address suggest?
options: A reason to post the name
A contact route that still needs safe verified procedure

quiz.question: What is the first duty after finding property?
options: Guard it securely before attempting return
